title: EIE CI and compliance catch-up to CEG parity
objective: Bring Quantum-L9/Enrichment.Inference.Engine main to CEG's CI/compliance level. The required org check Analyze (central Core) must be green with no false-positive-driven verdicts. main's Vulnerability Scan and OpenSSF Scorecard must be green. EIE must hold zero toolchain mismatches against Core, run hash-locked CI installs with a deterministic lock gate, isolate the networked SDK channel check, use precise pinned local Semgrep rules, SHA-pin its workflow actions, and drop dead workflows and scratch. All of this lands through fixes at each instrument's owner (l9-ci-sdk, l9-ci-core, EIE CI files) and never through EIE application-code edits or suppressions.

V6: central toolchain-alignment step on EIE reports 0 mismatches (baseline 8)
V7: lock --check exits 0 on main and 1 on a stale-lock negative-control test; every CI Python install uses --require-hashes
V8: EIE pytest suite passes with no new skip or xfail (baseline 3032 passed, 25 skipped, 4 xfailed)

disconfirming_questions: Does the narrowed token regex still catch access_token, refresh_tokens and auth token values passed to a logger?
Could the constant-only SQL rule miss f"... {user_input}" when the variable is UPPER_CASE by convention?
Do the receiver-scoped routing rules miss an L9 node call made through a generic httpx.post with a URL built from settings?
Can EIE PRs merge before the Core promotion, given that the required check is red on 25 app/ findings until T4?
Does publishing Dockerfile.prod break a deploy that relied on the DEV entrypoint's auto-migration?
Will SHA-pinning 96 refs conflict textually with PR-3/4/5 edits to the same workflow files?
assumed_false_ifs: the 27 findings contain a real secret, SQL or node-dispatch defect (audit: none; each read at file:line)
another governed repo depends on the over-broad rules for a real true positive (prototype: 0 delta across 4 repos)
stress_test.blast_radius: An SDK recall regression would silently stop blocking real secret logging or Gate bypass across every governed repo. A bad Core promotion reds every repo's required check. A wrong lock render breaks every EIE CI job. Dockerfile.prod publication changes the running production image.
stress_test.rollback: SDK: revert PR, Core keeps 6d70e829 as rollback-compatible revision; Core: revert step 2 then step 1; EIE PRs: each independently revertible by squash revert; PR-7: revert restores DEV-image publication

shared_causes: verdicts set by an owner other than the property they claim (rule over-approximation, local re-declaration of Core-owned versions, index-dependent lock render)
the dead or degraded instruments (dead caller, || true hook, missing permissions) report red or green without meaning
deletions_or_consolidations: delete EIE-local tool version drift (3 declarations collapse to Core pins)
